query: Consider the following context: The recent trend of high-entropy alloys (HEAs) was studied extensively for their promising mechanical properties, but individual constituents' effects have remained unexplored. In that context, which method can be used for the effects of changing the percentage of elements of HfNbTaTiZr-HEA on the mechanical properties, and why?

generation.hypothesis: Systematic variation of elemental percentages in HfNbTaTiZr-HEA will result in a change in mechanical properties due to the altered composition.
generation.material_initial_state: HfNbTaTiZr high-entropy alloy (HEA) with a uniform microstructure
generation.intervention: Systematic variation of elemental percentages (e.g., 10% increment/decrement of each element) using a controlled variable experiment
generation.conditions: Room temperature, ambient atmosphere, and a constant processing technique
generation.mechanism: Changes in elemental composition alter the grain size and lattice distortion, which in turn affect the mechanical properties (e.g., strength, hardness, and ductility)
generation.predicted_outcome: A 15% increase in yield strength (MPa) relative to the baseline composition (Hf20Nb20Ta20Ti20Zr20) when the Hf content is increased by 20% (Hf40Nb20Ta20Ti10Zr10)
generation.baseline: Hf20Nb20Ta20Ti20Zr20 composition with a yield strength of 1000 MPa
generation.boundary: Elemental percentages varied between 10% and 40% for each element
generation.uncertainty: The actual mechanical properties may vary depending on the specific processing technique and testing conditions used

falsification_experiment.design: Controlled variable experiment with systematic variation of elemental percentages
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the yield strength does not increase by at least 10% (i.e., 100 MPa) when the Hf content is increased by 20%, the hypothesis is falsified
